headline: High-risk default write-and-network pair: Plandex can modify local code and egress broadly, while awesome-nlp offers no isolation or runtime controls to constrain misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while Plandex uses a plan-local sandbox and stdin/stdout rather than ingesting outputs from another agent by default. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator copies awesome-nlp text into Plandex prompts, injection risk becomes possible.
IF either agent is connected through a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Disable any automation that forwards one agent's text into the other's prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, while Plandex reads and writes a project directory and can egress broadly. Without a shared workspace or sensitive data in scope, leakage is limited; the main concern is accidental exposure if both are pointed at the same files.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace containing secrets, Plandex can transmit those contents to external model providers.
IF the project directory includes regulated data, leakage severity increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running Plandex.
Set Plandex to a local/self-hosted model backend if available.
Review outbound network destinations before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The pair has overlapping filesystem write risk only through Plandex, which can write and modify git state, while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no write surface. The conflict is not symmetric, but if an orchestrator treats awesome-nlp artifacts as mutable project inputs, Plandex can overwrite or commit them without coordination.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git working tree, Plandex can create conflicting writes or commits.
IF an external orchestrator injects awesome-nlp-generated files into Plandex's project directory, write conflicts become plausible.
mitigations: Run Plandex in a separate clone.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same branch.
Pause auto-apply until changes are reviewed.
Use git locks or a single-writer workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references, and Plandex is explicitly a planner that can stage and apply changes. If Plandex consumes list-derived recommendations without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or plan changes.
conditions: IF Plandex uses awesome-nlp entries as factual authority without checking source quality, cascading error risk is present.
IF auto-apply is enabled, mistaken recommendations can become committed changes.
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on list entries.
Manually inspect any generated plan that cites awesome-nlp.
Restrict auto-apply for externally sourced recommendations.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is documented for awesome-nlp, and Plandex only explicitly handles source code and model-provider API keys. The pair does not show a residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of code and secrets.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared project directory, compliance review is needed.
IF Plandex is configured to send code to a third-party model provider under a stricter policy, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Use a self-hosted model backend where policy requires it.
Document retention for any generated plans.
